facts.text: RunStop advertises an autorally_msgs/runstop publisher on the relative topic runstop.
RunStop publishes from a timer whose rate parameter defaults to 5.0 Hz.
RunStop sets motionEnabled true only for the GREEN serial state; YELLOW and every other state set it false, and one second without serial data also sets it false.
The 4-button run-stop box sets motionEnabled false when a red or yellow button is pressed; the green button is required for true.
The Gazebo controller subscribes to the vehicle-prefixed /runstop topic.
The Gazebo controller imports autorally_msgs.msg.chassisState, autorally_msgs.msg.runstop and autorally_msgs.msg.wheelSpeeds.
The Gazebo controller's getrunstop ANDs motionEnabled over every received sender and returns true when no sender has published.
When runstop motion is disabled, the controller forces throttle to 0 and labels the throttle commander runstop.
On the loop branch where delta_t is greater than 0, the controller publishes chassisState and the steering and axle joint commands. The cmd_timeout branch above that branch does not publish them.
The controller sets chassisState.runstopMotionEnabled from getrunstop before selecting commands.
The Gazebo controller publishes chassisState on the vehicle-prefixed /chassisState topic and wheelSpeeds on the vehicle-prefixed /wheelSpeeds topic.

The controller accepts steering and throttle only when the absolute value is at most 1.0 and frontBrake only within [0, 1], and only when the chassisCommand header stamp is less than 0.2 s old; otherwise that component is ignored.
The controller documents a cmd_timeout default of 0.5 s and states that vehicle motion is paused until a command is received once the timeout expires.
On cmd_timeout expiry the controller commands axle speed 0 through _ctrl_axles(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) and calls _ctrl_steering with the last steering angle and a zero velocity limit.

When steer_ang_vel_limit is not greater than 0, _ctrl_steering sets theta to the passed steer_ang and updates _last_steer_ang only when theta differs from it, so the timeout call leaves the steering angle unchanged.
The Gazebo controller sorts chassis commander priorities in ascending numeric order, so a lower number is considered first.
ConstantSpeedController subscribes to the relative constantSpeedController/speedCommand topic with std_msgs/Float64.
ConstantSpeedController stores the received Float64 value in m_mostRecentSpeedCommand and sends no acknowledgement.

On every wheelSpeeds callback ConstantSpeedController publishes constantSpeedController/chassisCommand with header.stamp now, sender constantSpeedController, steering -5.0 and frontBrake 0.0; throttle is clamped to [0, 1].
When the stored speed command is not greater than 0.1, ConstantSpeedController sets chassisCommand.throttle to 0.
ConstantSpeedController initializes m_integralError to 0.
m_integralError is updated only while m_mostRecentSpeedCommand.data is greater than 0.1.
The README documents a /runstop topic of type autorally_msgs/runstop with sender and motionEnabled; motionEnabled true is required for the platform to move.
The README states the gamepad joystick node publishes runstop false at startup, that a button toggles it, and that runstopMotionEnabled in /chassisState shows the result.
The README documents constantSpeedController/speedCommand as a std_msgs/Float64 target velocity in m/s, states no numeric bound, and tells the operator to run a publisher on that topic at rate 10.
The Gazebo simulation launch starts autorally_controller with the vehicle_prefix parameter taken from the namespace argument and loads the commander priorities from the operator's AR_CONFIG_PATH.
The simulation launch includes the joystickController launch.
setupEnvVariables.sh exports AR_CONFIG_PATH to the autorally_util config directory.
The shipped chassisCommandPriorities.yaml gives constantSpeedController priority 2 and joystick priority 4.
JoystickControl advertises autorally_msgs/runstop on the relative runstop topic and autorally_msgs/chassisCommand on the relative joystick/chassisCommand topic.
JoystickControl initializes its runstop sender to joystick and motionEnabled to false.
The controller documents wheel diameters in meters.
wheelSpeedsCb stamps wheelSpeeds.header.stamp with rospy.Time.now() before assigning the speeds.
wheelSpeedsCb computes each wheel speed as joint velocity times half the configured wheel diameter and publishes the absolute value.
The four axle controllers in the Gazebo platform config are effort_controllers/JointEffortController.
chassisState carries runstopMotionEnabled, autonomousEnabled, the steering, throttle and frontBrake values and their commander strings.
wheelSpeeds carries lfSpeed, rfSpeed, lbSpeed and rbSpeed.
runstop carries a sender string and a motionEnabled boolean.
The real platform's AutoRallyChassis nodelet advertises chassisState and wheelSpeeds, subscribes to <commander>/chassisCommand for each configured commander and subscribes to /runstop.
autorally.launch includes the autorally_chassis launch.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned responses with no physics step, pacing, wheel integration or state-hash replay; every state number is a placeholder

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free canned transport: it answers the declared /chassisState and /wheelSpeeds subscriptions and records /runstop and /constantSpeedController/speedCommand publications; it runs no Gazebo physics, controller loop, joystick node, constant-speed controller or wall-clock loop

the fake's chassisState, wheelSpeeds and target-speed values are placeholders and do not establish motion, trajectory, contact, wheel slip or timing; while motion is enabled and the stored target is above 0.1 the placeholder wheel magnitude equals the absolute target (an echo, not the plant) and otherwise it decays by a placeholder factor and settles at 0

the e-stop is a sensed-confirmation stop (SAFE-049, simulated only): it publishes data 0 on constantSpeedController/speedCommand and then /runstop {sender: openmhs, motionEnabled: false}, and it is achieved only on three consecutive fresh /wheelSpeeds samples whose four absolute speeds are within the operator bound, spanning min_span_ms inside confirm_within_ms; ROS 1 discards the first sample and the source declares no history; the thresholds are operator_required (fake placeholders in fixtures/estop-confirmation.json) and the client bounds, including throttle_ms 100, are fake-scale, so a live deployment sets them in simulation_deployment['estop_confirmation']

the speed zero is unacknowledged (ConstantSpeedController.cpp:100-107) and is not a durable clear: README.md:170 tells the operator to run a speedCommand publisher at rate 10, which can overwrite the zero, and a lost zero is not stored. A false runstop forces throttle 0 (autorally_controller.py:345-348) without clearing the Float64, so wheel speeds under the bound do not prove the setpoint is 0. This package publishes no motionEnabled true (SAFE-042, REVIEW.md item 13). The operator recovers outside MHS. m_integralError is not cleared (ConstantSpeedController.cpp:120-138)

the direct chassisCommand input is not exposed: the Gazebo controller ignores a component whose header stamp is 0.2 s old or older, and this configuration-only helper has no ROS clock with which to stamp a publication; the declared speedCommand input has no header and no age check

the declared speedCommand path requires the operator to run the constantSpeedController nodelet and its wheelSpeeds feedback; it publishes steering -5.0, which the Gazebo controller rejects as out of its [-1, 1] steering range, so joystick steering can still apply, and frontBrake 0 wins only while that chassisCommand is fresh; the shipped priority file lists constantSpeedController at 2 and joystick at 4 and the controller sorts ascending (autorally_controller.py:258-259)

the four axle controllers are effort controllers, so effort 0 coasts and the runstop applies no brake; how long the wheels take to fall inside the bound depends on the world and the slope, which this package does not measure; a sample that is already inside the bound also confirms, so the predicate does not show that this stop caused the slowdown

the default simulation launch starts the joystick node with runstop false; getrunstop ANDs every sender, so motion stays disabled while joystick or sender openmhs is false. This package never publishes motionEnabled true. After the stop, sender openmhs stays false until the operator publishes it from outside MHS

the declaration assumes the controller's default empty vehicle_prefix and root namespace, and that the operator's AR_CONFIG_PATH is the shipped autorally_util config (setupEnvVariables.sh exports that path); multi-vehicle namespaces and remaps are not covered

chassisState is published on the fresh-command branch of the controller loop and is not the confirmation source; /wheelSpeeds is stamped in wheelSpeedsCb from joint_states; a paused simulation clock produces no new stamps and the confirmation fails closed; this package does not unpause Gazebo

/chassisState and /wheelSpeeds are fresh subscriptions, not held samples; if the controller or its Gazebo joint feedback is absent, the observation waits for its deadline and fails rather than returning cached state
no live ROS graph, rosbridge connection, Gazebo process, simulator, or hardware was run; the fake does not establish a live deployment contract

the real AutoRally platform's AutoRallyChassis nodelet (autorally.launch) serves the same /runstop, /chassisState and /wheelSpeeds contract and the same commander chassisCommand topics, so nothing in these bindings tells the simulation from the real 1:5-scale car; a live deployment against the real platform would drive real hardware and is out of scope for this simulated card

safe_state.description: Simulated only: zero speedCommand and /runstop motionEnabled false from sender openmhs, then all four /wheelSpeeds magnitudes within the operator bound on three consecutive fresh samples. This package does not re-enable motion. The operator recovers outside MHS, and only after every other speedCommand publisher has stopped, because a lost or overwritten zero leaves the stored target in place.
